title: Passive Se or Impersonal Se?
goal: Tell passive se, which agrees with a thing, from impersonal se, which stays singular.
grammar: Passive se, impersonal se and personal a

items: I can tell passive se, which agrees with a thing, from impersonal se, which stays singular.
I can keep the verb singular when a particular person follows with personal a.
I can use the new words for people in charge, customers and neighbours.
